## Paper

- [Hypergraph-Enhanced Evidence Selection for Long-Context Multimodal Document QA](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35542) — document-vqa, formula-recognition: Long-context multimodal document question answering (QA) has become an important yet challenging task for modern vision-language models (VLMs), as it requires reasoning over evidence dispersed across pages and modalities within limited input budgets. Current pipelines adopt retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to select multimodal evidence for downstream VLMs. However, existing systems mainly rely on static selection rules over fixed-granularity retrieval units such as pages or blocks, resulting in information loss during retrieval and suboptimal performance in downstream reasoning. To alleviate these issues, we formulate the core task as budget-aware evidence selection over structured document evidence and propose HyperDoc, a document RAG framework that constructs compact yet sufficient evidence while preserving document relations. Specifically, HyperDoc constructs a document hypergraph to explicitly capture structural, logical, and cross-modal relationships among multimodal document elements. Over this structured evidence space, HyperDoc performs adaptive cost-aware hyperedge selection based on query intent and input budget. Extensive experiments on three representative benchmarks demonstrate that HyperDoc outperforms various types of state-of-the-art baselines.- [LayoutMamba: Efficient Document Layout Analysis with Hybrid Mamba-Transformer Networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34879) — document-layout-analysis: Document layout analysis (DLA) faces a long-standing dilemma: existing methods either capture rich local details at prohibitive computational cost (e.g., Transformer-based approaches with quadratic complexity) or achieve efficient global modeling but sacrifice fine-grained structural awareness (e.g., state-space models). This trade-off hinders deployment in resource-constrained scenarios. We present LayoutMamba, a hybrid framework that synergistically combines sparse-attention Transformers for localized feature extraction (O(n) complexity) and the recurrent state-space mechanism of Mamba for dilution-free long-range dependency modeling across the 2D document canvas. Our two-stage paradigm first uses a lightweight Transformer encoder to hierarchically distill salient local semantics; second, Mamba propagates global contextual dependencies without attention dilution, enabling precise, efficient, and scalable layout understanding. We further identify a critical yet overlooked issue in existing DLA benchmarks: the inherent low-overlap distribution bias of layout objects, which we mitigate through a novel Geometric Overlap Penalty Loss (GOPLoss), a dual-optimization objective that minimizes redundant bounding box overlaps and encourages geometrically consistent predictions. Extensive experiments on PubLayNet and D4LA show that LayoutMamba surpasses state-of-the-art AP on PubLayNet with 8x fewer parameters and maintains leading performance on D4LA, ranking top-3 among published methods, achieving an unprecedented balance between accuracy, efficiency, and scalability. Our work pioneers a cognition-inspired paradigm for document analysis, advancing practical deployment in edge computing and resource-limited environments.- [MuSTEL: A Large-Scale Multilingual Synthetic Text-Line Image Dataset for OCR](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34148) — text-recognition: Optical character recognition (OCR) systems depend strongly on the scale and diversity of their training data. One approach to document OCR first analyzes the page layout and extracts text-line images, which are then transcribed by a recognition model. Multilingual line-level recognition involving Persian, Arabic, and English presents additional challenges because different writing directions, fonts, and styles may coexist within a single line. This paper introduces MuSTEL, a large-scale synthetic multilingual OCR dataset containing more than 14.5 million annotated text-line images, organized into a training partition and predefined small and large test sets. Samples are generated from natural-language corpora, including multilingual content already present in the source texts. The generation framework incorporates capability-aware font selection, within-line font and style changes, mixed-direction text rendering, highlighting, and underlining. A validated repository of 2,009 font files from 711 families supports broad typographic coverage, while varied backgrounds, blur, geometric distortion, skew, stroke width, and image save quality provide diverse document-like appearances. Statistical analysis characterizes the dataset's language composition, transcription lengths, lexical and character-sequence diversity, image dimensions, typography, and rendering conditions. MuSTEL provides a resource for training and evaluating multilingual line-level OCR systems and investigating recognition robustness across languages, writing directions, and visual conditions.
